findings.title: Adoption resolver failures can be returned as successful error-context builds
findings.description: The integrator rethrows `AdoptionError` but converts other exceptions into an error-context string. Some adoption failures are not wrapped as `AdoptionError`: for example, `readAdoptionState` explicitly lets malformed TOML parser errors propagate. In that case, `cf build` can return the error context instead of failing, contrary to the adoption resolver’s fail-explicitly behavior. Ensure failures from adoption resolution are surfaced rather than converted into a successful build result.

findings.title: Adoption state is persisted before facts are gathered
findings.description: The resolver writes `in_progress` before calling `renderFacts`. That call performs filesystem checks through `presentPaths` and `recognizeCi`, which can throw on filesystem errors. If it does, the build can fail or produce the integrator’s error stub after the state has already changed; the next build then treats adoption as in progress. Gather the required facts successfully before persisting, or otherwise ensure a failed build does not leave the adoption state changed.
